newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot under assault from ex-comrades -Ranariddh.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot under assault from ex-comrades -Ranariddh.

text.p: Hated Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot offered to surrender but former comrades-in-arms refused and are making a final assault to capture him, Cambodia's first prime minister said on Friday.
"They finally know where he is and will make a final assault today in the hope we will be able to capture Pol Pot alive," Prince Norodom Ranariddh told reporters.
Ranariddh said Pol Pot was holed up with 15 people who he would not identify. He said he knew the location but would not reveal it.
"I have heard clearly this morning that Pol Pot offered to surrender but the forces around him don't want him to surrender," he said.

Asked why the forces opposing Pol Pot would not accept his surrender, Ranariddh said: "There is a great difference between surrender and capture. Surrender means we have to give Pol Pot safe conduct," he said. "We have to capture him alive."
Ranariddh called for Pol Pot to be placed on trial for the death of more than one million Cambodians during his "killing fields" rule of Cambodia from 1975 to 1979.
